definitions.observable_time: cycle: day of last (closing) edge; fan_in/fan_out: day the k-th distinct counterparty has transacted (k=observable_k), else last transaction day
definitions.warning_time: earliest day any transaction of the ring is flagged by the daily budget (out-of-sample days only)
definitions.lead_time: observable_day - warning_day, in days; >0 means warned before the ring became observable
definitions.evaluable_ring: ALL transactions of the ring fall inside the scored period (first_day >= first scored day) and its observable_day is scored; this avoids right-truncating warnings. The JSON also keeps summary_observable_in_period (only observable_day in the scored period), which is truncated for slow rings.

caveats: AMLSim-specific shortcut: ring members are drawn from otherwise-dormant accounts, so 'first-ever sender' transactions are almost always ring transactions after a warm-up. xgb_without_novelty uses same-day information only (no account history); newness_rule is a two-bit rule (first-ever sender / first-ever receiver); random is a control. If xgb_with_novelty does not clearly beat newness_rule, the model adds nothing beyond the shortcut.
Labels are used only as training targets for rows before each scored block and for evaluation.
Rings that continue into a scored block are excluded from that block's training set (ring-grouped split).
Daily timestamps: a flag on the same day as observable_time gives lead 0 (not early).
Evaluable ring counts are small for some typologies; read N and the confidence intervals.

protocol.model_blocks: one model per 120-day block, trained only on earlier data

definitions.observable_time: cycle: day of the closing (last) edge; fan: day the 4-th distinct counterparty has transacted
definitions.warning_time: first day the candidate's risk score (computed only from evidence up to that day) reaches the alert threshold and the candidate contains a transaction of the ring
definitions.lead_time: observable_day - warning_day in days; positive = warned before the ring was complete
definitions.evaluable_ring: all transactions of the ring fall in the scored period (first day >= scored_from) and it completes inside the data

caveats: AMLSim-specific shortcut: ring members are drawn from otherwise-dormant accounts, so first-time accounts are unusually informative here.
Only cycle rings are fully evaluable: fan rings take longer than the data allows to start and finish inside the scored period.
Warnings arrive with the ring's first transactions, so lead is measured against ring completion, not against a ring's start.
Labels are used only to train earlier blocks and to evaluate; never to build candidates or scores.
